messages:
noah: Quick heads-up — linkcheck is tripping on pages where a numbered list immediately follows a top-level heading. Anchor ends up with a -1 suffix.
anya: Can you paste a tiny repro?
noah: Minimal repro:
```markdown
# Getting started
1. Create project
2. Start server

See: [getting started](#getting-started)
```
ci-bot: linkcheck/job/512 failed: ERROR anchor not found: /get-started#getting-started -> resolved to /get-started#getting-started-1
frank: Huh. Some parsers generate implicit ids for list items or do slug dedupe differently when numbered lists are present. Two quick fixes: insert a blank line between heading and list, or add an explicit id on the heading.
anya: Try the blank line first — less invasive. If that works, open a PR to sanitize pages during migration.
noah: Blank line fixed it locally. I'll open a tiny PR: add `docs/testing/numbered-list-anchor.md` with repro, update mkdocs.yml to enable attr_list, and a CI linkcheck assertion so we catch regressions. Tagging @frank for review. :eyes:
ci-bot: linkcheck/job/512 re-run queued for branch: fix/numbered-list-anchor
frank: Also worth adding a short note in the migration guide advising maintainers to avoid inline numbered lists directly after headings or to prefer explicit `{#id}`. Small manual change but saves future surprises.
noah: Agreed — will add migration blurb and a test page. Thanks all! :thumbsup:
